html:
SMTO-TSK-0063 — This task is waiting for an earlier task that didn't succeed

GUID: 61e72149-ef2f-47ac-aa84-ae0c1c5b3a1c
Slug: task-dependency-unsatisfied
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • This task was set to run only after another task finished successfully. That earlier task hasn't succeeded, or SMTO can't find it, so this task hasn't started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find the task in the conversation and read its Waiting on note to see which earlier task it depends on. That earlier task decides when this one can start.
  2. If the earlier task is still running or waiting for you, let it finish or answer what it asks. This task starts by itself once the earlier one completes successfully.
  3. If the earlier task failed or was stopped, read what it already did before running it again, so work isn't done twice. It may have finished part of its work before it stopped.
  4. After you've checked what the earlier task did, if you want this task to run anyway, select Start task on it in the queue while it shows Dependency blocked. This runs only this task without waiting; other tasks still wait as set.

What success looks like

  • The task's status changes to Running and its results appear in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't send the same request again as a new task while the earlier one is unresolved; you could end up doing the work twice.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Dependency evaluation for this task is not satisfied: a predecessor is still pending or ended failed, cancelled or interrupted, or is missing, deleted, invalid or part of a cycle, and no explicit skip applies.

What this means

  • Canonical dependency evaluation is not satisfied, including pending, failed/cancelled/interrupted, missing, invalid or cyclic predecessor state without an applicable explicit skip. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Canonical dependency evaluation is not satisfied, including pending, failed/cancelled/interrupted, missing, invalid or cyclic predecessor state without an applicable explicit skip.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the dependency projection's root task and reason rather than assuming all blockers are still running.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the predecessor's actual status and receipts (the task's Waiting on / Dependency blocked detail). If it is still running, wait; if it failed or was cancelled, review its effects, then rerun or complete it, or use Start task (start-blocked) to waive the edge for this task only. Do not resubmit work while the predecessor's outcome is unresolved.
  • Inspect the actual predecessor state and use existing recovery or explicit dependency controls after reviewing its effects.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Prerequisites complete or an explicit supported scoped override is recorded; unrelated edges remain enforced.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
